report.answer_text:
On March 1, 2025, NASA’s Europa Clipper flew about 550 miles (884 kilometers) above Mars, using the planet’s gravity to bend its trajectory toward Jupiter. During the flyby, it took infrared images of Mars to calibrate its thermal camera and tested its ice-penetrating radar as a complete system for the first time. (science.nasa.gov)
Europa Clipper is scheduled to enter orbit around Jupiter in April 2030. (science.nasa.gov)
